q: The universal coefficient theorem for cohomology relates H^n(X; G) to homology via:
opts: 0 → Ext¹(H_{n-1}(X), G) → H^n(X;G) → Hom(Hₙ(X), G) → 0 (split, not naturally)
exp: Universal coefficient theorem: H^n(X;G) fits in a split short exact sequence 0 → Ext¹(H_{n-1}(X),G) → H^n(X;G) → Hom(H_n(X),G) → 0. The Ext term captures the 'torsion' correction. For G = ℤ, the Ext term picks up torsion in H_{n-1}(X).
